{"answers":[{"question_id":"Q004_ferritin_like_functional_divergence","answer":"SCOPe interprets these proteins as divergent relatives with different chemistries. In release 2.08, discovered as the current release, Ferritin (a.25.1.1; sunid 47241), Ribonucleotide reductase-like (a.25.1.2; 47253), and Manganese catalase (T-catalase) (a.25.1.3; 100951) are separate families within the Ferritin-like superfamily (a.25.1; 47240). This superfamily belongs to the Ferritin-like fold (a.25; 47239), in the All alpha proteins class (a; 46456).

Their shared superfamily expresses inferred common evolutionary ancestry despite potentially weak sequence similarity. Family membership indicates a closer relationship; fold membership alone describes a shared structural arrangement without necessarily implying homology, and class membership describes secondary-structure composition. Here the relationship is therefore stronger than merely sharing an all-alpha fold.

The conserved ferritin-like helical scaffold supports differing metal-dependent functions: ferritins oxidize and store iron; canonical class I ribonucleotide reductase R2 proteins generate the radical cofactor that supports nucleotide reduction in the partner catalytic subunit; manganese catalases use a binuclear manganese center to disproportionate hydrogen peroxide into water and oxygen. The Ribonucleotide reductase-like family label does not mean every member performs ribonucleotide reduction, nor does it classify every ribonucleotide reductase catalytic subunit as ferritin-like.

Different metal ligands, active-site environments, substrate access, and assembly can produce these functional differences on an ancestral scaffold. Thus neither homology nor the superfamily name licenses transfer of iron-storage function, radical chemistry, catalase activity, metal specificity, or oligomeric state across these families. A distant member may provide a template for the conserved structural core, but detailed functional annotation requires sequence and active-site comparisons, metal/cofactor evidence, and biochemical characterization. Representatives should cover the distinct families and relevant functional subgroups; a single ferritin cannot represent the superfamily's chemical diversity.","evidence_used":["Pretrained model knowledge","/api/v1/","/api/v1/releases/2.08/search?q=ferritin","/api/v1/releases/2.08/sunids/47241","/api/v1/releases/2.08/sunids/47240","/api/v1/releases/2.08/resolve/a.25.1.2","/api/v1/releases/2.08/resolve/a.25.1.3","/api/v1/releases/2.08/sunids/47239","/api/v1/releases/2.08/search?q=Ribonucleotide%20reductase-like&limit=5","/api/v1/releases/2.08/sunids/47263","/api/v1/releases/2.08/sunids/190435","/api/v1/releases/2.08/sunids/100951","/api/v1/releases/2.08/sunids/46456","/api/v1/releases/2.08/sunids/47253"]}]}
